scenarios.title: Two devices edit the same cart
scenarios.description: A user changes an item quantity on a phone while removing the same item on a laptop at nearly the same time.
probes: What final state does the user see and is it acceptable?
How does your design detect the conflict?
Would operation-based updates change the outcome?

scenarios.title: Flash sale on a single product
scenarios.description: Millions of shoppers add the same limited-stock product to carts within minutes.
probes: Which component becomes the hot spot: cart store, catalog cache, or inventory?
Does adding to cart reserve stock and what happens to abandoned reservations?
How do users learn the item sold out?

scenarios.title: Pricing service is unavailable
scenarios.description: The pricing or catalog dependency errors while users view their carts.
probes: Can users still view and edit carts? What do they see for prices?
How do you prevent checkout at a wrong price?
Which timeouts, fallbacks, and circuit breakers are in place?

scenarios.title: Payment fails after handoff
scenarios.description: The cart has been handed to checkout, and payment fails or times out.
probes: What state is the cart in and can the user continue editing?
How do you avoid creating two orders if the client retries?
What happens to any reserved inventory?

scenarios.title: Stale cart in cache
scenarios.description: A cart cached in one region does not reflect a change just made from another device.
probes: How stale can the cart be and is that acceptable?
Which invalidation strategy do you use and what happens when invalidation fails?
Does checkout read from the cache or the source of truth?
